cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Fake the Expertise
cards.instruction: Perform expertise so confidently that no one questions you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. I'll tune your violin for the audition. I work by ear.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've tightened that string until it snapped.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. That string couldn't hold pitch. I've saved you a failure onstage.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The audition panel heard it snap. They're asking if you know what you're doing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell them I rejected an unreliable string. Ask for their spare violin; I'll check that one before I approve it.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 sets decision power, A3 defers challenge, and A5 demands a replacement for personal approval while performing expert rejection of the broken string.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 snapped string causes A3 quality-control cover; B4 panel scrutiny causes A5 a revised report and request for another instrument.

relationship.evidence: B2 reports damage and B4 conveys the panel concern, plausibly protecting an imminent audition.

heightening.evidence: B4 wider exposure produces A5 a bolder demand to inspect the panel spare rather than surrender authority.

specificity.evidence: A1 violin audition and B2 breakage establish immediate stakes; B4 introduces the panel listening.
